title: Finite-dimensional representations of the classical groups, Part II: Rational symplectic-similitude characters
summary: Rational algebraic representations of split GSp₂g over Q and their integral torus characters. The plan extends the complex classical-group theory by the central-similitude lattice, rational forms and scalar extension, then identifies the full character ring and the subring generated by simple constituents of tensor powers of the standard representation. Pure invariant algebra is independent of representation theory. Its central twist records the difference between multiplier degree and scalar degree, and its rational-to-complex comparison uses finite comodule base change rather than an abstract point-group character theorem.
readme: This Part II begins with the complex connected classical-group highest-weight and character theory of its parent, and adds rational algebraic GSp representations and the central multiplier variable. Its target is Yu’s Remark 7.1.1. For g≥1 it identifies R(GSp₂g/Q) with Z[t±1,z_i±1]^W, where reciprocal swaps send z_i to t/z_i, and identifies the subring generated by simple constituents of standard tensor powers with Z[z_i,t/z_i]^W. The full ring is polynomial in the primitive exterior characters over Z[t±1]; the constituent ring is polynomial in those characters and t over Z. The elementary invariant algebra is independent of representation theory. Arithmetic Statistics owns the general matrix similitude group, Reductive Groups owns Hopf/representation foundations and quotient descent, and the parent classical roadmap owns the connected Sp highest-weight, character and dimension results. This roadmap specializes and joins those inputs; it does not reconstruct them. It works in characteristic zero, includes negative multiplier twists in the full rational category, and takes g≥1 so that the multiplier is unique. Finite-field representation categories, smooth representations of p-adic point groups and characteristic-p semisimplicity are outside its scope.

stages.title: Algebraic similitudes, diagonal torus and central weights
stages.description: Represent the imported matrix GSp group by its explicit finite-type coordinate Hopf algebra. Construct the diagonal torus and central-similitude lattice Z×Z^g, register its reciprocal Weyl action, and prove the central isogeny Sp₂g×G_m→GSp₂g with μ₂ kernel, its parity/descent criterion and the split connected reductive root datum. Check rank one, the multiplier-one fibre and non-surjectivity of the cover on Q-points.

stages.title: Rational algebraic representations and primitive powers
stages.description: Specialize the existing finite-comodule category and SplitK0 to GSp. Construct standard and multiplier representations, primitive exterior powers with ν-valued contraction, and their split decomposition and fundamental highest weights. Prove the finite Hom/weight base-change theorem, construct the rational highest tensor component using semisimplicity and its one-dimensional top line, and classify rational irreducibles with unrestricted integer multiplier exponent. Induce the canonical Q-to-C and Q-to-K ring equivalence using the existing SplitK0 functorial map.

stages.title: Integral torus characters and the full representation ring
stages.description: Construct the integer formal torus character using existing weight spaces and SplitK0.liftRingHom. Prove algebraic highest-weight injectivity, define the fundamental exterior polynomials with the signed-degree convention, construct the integral full invariant polynomial presentation, and identify the primitive characters. Prove Yu’s canonical rational character ring isomorphism and the full polynomial generators over Z[t±1].

stages.title: Tensor constituents and the positive character algebra
stages.description: Define the elementary reciprocal Laurent subring by its monomial generators and prove the precise exponent-support cone, independently of representations. Construct its integral invariant polynomial presentation. Define the ring generated by simple algebraic tensor-power constituents, prove the exact highest-weight occurrence criterion m≥0 at degree 2m+Σu_i, and identify that ring with the positive invariants. Establish integral generation by ν and the primitive exterior expressions and recover the full rational ring by inverting ν.
